patch.pni: Present, 0.1 mm or more in calibre

report:
Skin, scalp (midline), excision

Received in formalin is an ellipse of skin measuring 3.5 x 2.0 x 1.0 cm bearing an ulcerated nodule measuring 1.5 cm. A suture marks 12 o'clock, taken as superior. The lesion is 4 mm from the closest skin edge. The deep surface is inked. The ellipse is serially sliced and all embedded in 5 blocks.

(1) Tip A. (2-4) Lesion, cross-sections. (5) Tip B.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Excision
- Tumour site: Scalp (midline)
- Tumour size: 15 mm (greatest dimension)

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: Squamous cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified
- Histologic grade: G3, poorly differentiated
- Tumour histology:
  The tumour is a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, invading the subcutaneous fat to a depth of 7 mm. It is composed of cords and sheets of pleomorphic cells with frequent mitoses, squamous differentiation being evident only as rare intercellular bridges or small foci of keratinisation. The tumour cells express p40 and CK5/6 and are negative for SOX10.
- Depth of invasion: 7 mm
- Anatomic level: V (carcinoma invades subcutaneum)
- Lymphovascular invasion: Not identified
- Perineural invasion: Present, 0.1 mm or more in calibre

Margins
- Invasive tumour: All margins negative
  - Closest peripheral margin: 5 mm (posterior)
  - Deep margin: 1 mm

Pathological stage (AJCC 8th edition)
- pTNM: pT3

BWH tumour classification
- BWH class: T2b: 2-3 high-risk factors
  - High-risk factors: Poorly differentiated histology and perineural invasion
    0.1 mm or more in calibre

Additional findings
- None identified

SKIN, scalp (midline), excision
- SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA, poorly differentiated, 15 mm, invading the
  subcutaneous fat to a depth of 7 mm; perineural invasion present (0.1 mm or
  more in calibre); completely excised (closest peripheral margin 5 mm,
  posterior; deep margin 1 mm); see synoptic report
- pT3 (AJCC 8th edition); BWH T2b
